$comment: THE hand-written part. Four packages are generated from this directory and are never edited. Discord's first-party v10 reference and its generated stable OpenAPI preview are the sources; where they disagree, Discord explicitly says the prose documentation wins.
title: Discord

authorize.$comment: A bot token authenticates as the application's dedicated bot user, not as a human through OAuth2. Discord requires the literal `Bot ` scheme; using Bearer would describe a user OAuth token and a different permission model.

$sandboxComment: Discord has no alternate REST host or synthetic message estate. Its own tutorial requires a server for testing, so isolation is a dedicated test server and development-only application using the same v10 API.
sandboxNote: Create a development-only Discord application, install its bot into a dedicated test server, and use a test channel id. Messages are real and can notify members of that server; production credentials sent in sandbox mode are not technically rejected.
idempotencyNote: Discord accepts a string nonce of at most 25 characters. With enforce_nonce true it deduplicates messages from the same author only within the past few minutes, returning the original message; this is a short retry window, not a permanent uniqueness guarantee.

credentialFields.label: Bot token
credentialFields.help: The token from the application's Bot page. Treat it as a password and install that bot into the target server with Send Messages permission.
